Context: `ultext(Source Information)`: Kale was an `text(11-year-old)` African boy on board the Amistad. While in prison in New Haven, abolitionists taught him to read and write in English. This excerpt is from a `text(3-page)` letter he wrote to John Quincy Adams on `text(January 4, 1841)`. Adams was a former U.S. president and lawyer who had been asked by leading abolitionists to defend the Amistad men in front of the Supreme Court.
Title: Source D
Content: :box:I want to write a letter to you because you love Mendi people, and you talk to the grand court... Mendi people been in America `17` moons [months]. We talk American language a little, not very good... We want you to ask the Court what we have done wrong... We want to be free very much... If America gives us free we glad, if they no give us free we sorry — we sorry for Mendi people little, we sorry for America people great deal because God punish liars... If Court ask who bring Mendi people to America, we bring ourselves... Send us home... We tell them there is `text(one)` god. You must worship him. Make us free and we will bless you and all Mendi people will bless you. Dear friend Mr. Adams.
